You will direct really strong video editors and UGC creators, and you will use AI (including Claude Code) as your production engine for research, hooks, scripts and variants. You will get mentorship, a proven creative system, and weekly learnings reviews. In return we expect pace, curiosity, and work you can defend.

What you will do

  • Build the research base first: homeowner avatars, desires, objections, competitors, and our own ad account history. No angles before research.

  • Plan concepts in a structured roadmap, each with angle, avatar, desire, mechanism, authority, awareness level, emotion, positioning and urgency.

  • Write hooks and scripts built for the first 3 seconds: one desire, one avatar, one message per ad.

  • Brief UGC creators and editors so clearly they can execute with no follow-up call, and review their work to a finished, launch-ready ad.

  • Run the testing system: from one winning angle, build structured iterations where each variation tests something named.

  • Run the learnings: label every ad (Breakthrough, Spend Winner, KPI Winner, Loser), state why it performed, and turn that into the next round.

  • Hit 20 to 30 finished, launch-ready ads per month at full pace, working with our editors and AI workflows.

What we are looking for

  • Direct-response ad experience: you have written ads that ran as paid social (Meta or TikTok) and you can show them.

  • A testing system, not just good taste. You can explain how you turn one winner into 20 variations.

  • Research discipline. Your hooks trace to evidence, not guesses.

  • AI fluency: you already use AI tools in your creative workflow and can show how.

  • Execution: you have briefed creators or managed editors and shipped finished ads.

  • Ownership mindset: you talk about business outcomes, not just outputs delivered, and you close feedback loops: you learn, you apply, you show what changed.

  • Local services or lead generation experience is a plus, not a requirement. Seasonal urgency, emergency calls, proof and trust are the game here.

Pay and structure

  • Contract (1099), remote, month-to-month: $4,000 to $8,000 per month, 40 hours per week, based on experience.

  1. Short application: portfolio of ads you wrote that actually ran, plus 3 short answers (your testing system on a real winner; one ad you iterated and what it tested; your AI workflow).

  2. Interview 1 (30 minutes): screening and craft in one call, run as a working session on your past ads: what did you learn, how did you apply it, what feedback loops did you complete.

  3. Paid test: $100 flat, 48 hours, capped at 4 hours of work, paid regardless of outcome. A short research snapshot, hooks, scripts, an iteration plan and an execution plan for a real scenario.

  4. Interview 2 (final, with the owner): we walk your test together and you defend your choices. References are checked after this call (we will ask to speak with one past employer). Two interviews total, no more.

  5. Paid 30-day trial at your full agreed monthly rate, with daily contact, mentorship and a weekly check-in. Written decision at day 30.

We hire off the test and the trial, not the interview. If you are the kind of strategist who would rather prove it than pitch it, apply.

You will own the day-to-day operation of the program and work directly with our General Counsel, our CEO, our Head of Operations and the outside lobbyists and local counsel we retain.

The Role

The Regulatory Affairs Manager runs Swimply's regulatory program end to end. Half of the job is operational: every notice a host or the company receives is logged, answered and tracked to a close. The other half is strategic: finding the bills, partners and officials that let us fix the rules for a whole state at once instead of town by town.

Run the notice program

  • Own the regulatory intake: the regulatory inbox, the host reporting form and escalations from the Host Success team.
  • Log every cease-and-desist letter, notice of violation, HOA demand and listing takedown in the regulatory tracker, by state, city, issuing agency and legal theory.
  • Sort each matter by the theory being used against us: public pool classification, home occupation or zoning, short-term rental rules, business licensing and tax, or HOA covenants.
  • Send the approved standard response to the host or code officer, and follow up until the matter is closed or escalated.
  • Escalate to the General Counsel within one business day anything involving a subpoena, a records demand, a lawsuit, criminal exposure or a threat to a whole market.
  • Publish a weekly regulatory report for the CEO and General Counsel: new notices, open matters, trends and recommended next steps.

Change the rules, state by state

  • Track bills and ordinances in our priority states, starting with New Jersey, New York, California and Texas, and flag any short-term rental or health-code bill our language could be added to.
  • Keep our model state bill and model city ordinance current.
  • Prepare the testimony, one-pagers, fact sheets and talking points our lobbyists and executives use with legislators and staff.
  • Reach out directly to selected city planning, code enforcement and health departments to explain our safety standards before a problem starts.
  • Manage outside firms and budget.
  • Day-to-day manager for our lead lobbying firm, state lobbyists and local zoning counsel: scopes, weekly updates, deadlines and invoices.
  • Build and maintain a bench of zoning counsel and lobbyists in each problem state, ready for when a matter escalates.
  • Own the regulatory budget against the plan the board approves, and give leadership a clear cost-versus-outcome view before any new engagement is signed.

Build allies

  • Represent Swimply in short-term rental coalitions, state chambers of commerce, realtor associations and pool and spa industry groups.
  • Recruit and prepare hosts to speak at hearings and council meetings.

Keep us compliant

  • Handle lobbying registrations and periodic disclosure filings at the state and city level.
  • Support Finance on offers to collect and remit local taxes in jurisdictions that confirm our legality in writing.
  • Research permit, occupancy and licensing requirements for new products and new markets, including Canada, and brief the General Counsel and product teams.
  • Pull and organize platform data when counsel needs it to respond to a government request.

Required

  • Hands-on experience with how state legislatures and city councils actually move a bill or ordinance: committees, staff, hearings and timing.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, AI Coding Tasks

We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

How it works

  1. Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
  2. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.
  3. Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.
  4. Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
  5. Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
  6. Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.
  7. Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.

Requirements

  • 2+ years of professional software engineering
  • Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)
  • Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++
  • Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing
  • Regular use of an AI coding tool
  • Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models
  • You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words
  • At least 10 hours a week, starting now

Nice to have

  • Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure
  • Experience building agent tasks or RL environments

Terms

  • Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms
  • The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us
